name: The Nature and Ranks of Angels
path: Angelology: The Doctrine of Spiritual Beings

objectives.text: Identify angels as spirits that God created
Explain that the word angel means messenger and name Gabriel as an angel God sent with a message
Recall from Scripture that angels are usually invisible to people and are mighty in strength
Describe the scenes in Isaiah and Revelation where angels worship God around His throne
Summarize what angels are as created, spiritual, and personal beings with mind and will
Explain that angels are a distinct kind of creature from humans and that people do not become angels when they die
Compare the power and knowledge of angels with that of humans and with the unlimited power and knowledge of God
Categorize the kinds of angels Scripture names, including cherubim, seraphim, and the archangel
Identify Michael and Gabriel as the only angels named in the canonical Scriptures and describe what the texts say about each
Analyze the role of the cherubim as guardians of God's holy presence in Eden, the tabernacle, and Ezekiel's vision
Explain how Paul's terms thrones, dominions, rulers, and authorities point to ordered ranks of spiritual beings created by and subject to Christ
Interpret Old Testament scenes of the divine council in which God presides over the assembly of spiritual beings
Connect the vast number of angels described in Scripture to the greatness and majesty of God
Explain the Reformed teaching that the holy angels are elect and confirmed in holiness
Explain from Hebrews 1 why the Son is superior to the angels in nature and rank
Analyze the angel of the LORD passages and evaluate the view held by many Reformed interpreters that some are appearances of the pre-incarnate Son
Explain from Scripture why angels, as fellow creatures, must not be worshiped
Evaluate popular cultural and sentimental ideas about angels against the teaching of Scripture
Defend the reality of an unseen created spiritual realm against naturalistic objections
Compare the restraint of Reformed angelology with speculative medieval hierarchies such as the nine choirs of angels
Construct a summary of the biblical doctrine of the nature, ranks, and moral state of the holy angels drawn from the whole of Scripture

changes: Fixed the Jude reference to Jude 1:9. Kept and reworded the real competencies on creation, invisibility, worship, nature, kinds of angels, cherubim, divine council, multitude, moral state, myths, and naturalism. Merged the two whole-Scripture synthesis objectives into one grade 12 construction task. Added objectives on named angels, Pauline ranks under Christ, the superiority of the Son in Hebrews 1, the angel of the LORD, the prohibition of angel worship, limits of angelic knowledge, and medieval speculative hierarchies. Added anchors from WCF 3.3 and Belgic Confession Article 12. Left angelic service, Satan, demons, and victory to the sibling sub-topics.
